workout.session_type: Lower Body - Full Session (training around right scapular strain)
workout.warmup: 10 min incline walk (3.3-3.5 mph, 6-8%). Then 90/90 hip switches x 10/side, bodyweight glute bridge x 15, Cat-Cow x 10. Ramp the squat: bar + 45/side x 8, then 70/side x 3.
workout.coach_note: I had this wrong and you corrected me, so here is the revised plan. I read your injury as a lumbar strain and built you a rehab day. It is not lumbar - it is your RIGHT MID-BACK, under the shoulder blade. That is the same place you strained on June 9, which makes this a recurrence, not a new injury. It also means your legs are completely uninvolved: you squatted 185 for 7/7/7 and hinged on Sunday with no back problem, which is the proof. So you do not need a rest day. You need a full lower body session with your upper back left alone. Look at what actually provokes it: hoisting a 50 lb DB to your knee on Friday, and the lat pulldown yesterday. Both are loaded scapular retraction and depression. Bench pressing yesterday was pain-free. So PULLING aggravates it, pressing does not, and legs do not touch it at all. Today is heavy legs and zero loaded pulling. The one change from a normal lower day is the hinge: back extension instead of RDL, because a loaded barbell hangs from your shoulder girdle and puts traction right through the strained tissue. Your leg curl also gets the 80 lb it earned on Aug 16. One more thing, and I mean this: same muscle, twice in ten weeks, both times from a dumbbell setup. That is a pattern, not bad luck, and it is worth twenty minutes with a physical therapist to find out why that area keeps failing. I can program around it indefinitely but I cannot diagnose it.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
exercises.note: Same load as Sunday, chasing reps instead of weight. You got 7/7/7 at 185 on Aug 23 and 6/6/7 on Aug 16 - it is moving the right direction, so bank a clean 4x8 before we load it again. Brace before you unrack. One note specific to your injury: setting the bar on your back requires you to pull your shoulder blades together to build a shelf, so if that position lights up the right side, use a slightly wider grip and a lighter squeeze. Report if it does.

exercises.name: 45-Degree Back Extension - REPLACES RDL
exercises.detail: Bodyweight, arms crossed on chest - 3 x 15
exercises.note: Bodyweight ONLY today and arms crossed on the chest - do not hold a plate and do not hold a dumbbell. The whole point is a hinge with zero load hanging from your shoulder girdle, because a loaded bar drags the scapula down through exactly the tissue you strained. Pad at the hip crease, not the belly. Squeeze glutes and hamstrings up to a straight line, no arching past neutral, slow 3-second lower. Your lumbar spine handled hinging fine on Sunday so this should feel easy - that is intentional.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.note: THE BUMP YOU EARNED. You put up 70 x 12/12/12 on Aug 16, which is what I had been asking for across three sessions. First time at 80, so take what it gives you - 10 clean reps a set is a win. Hamstrings faded badly on Sunday (12/10/7), but that was after four sets of squats plus RDLs; today's hinge is far less taxing so they should show up better.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust Machine
exercises.note: Back in the rotation - you have not trained glutes directly since the kickback machine on Aug 16, which you correctly hated. Full hip extension, hard squeeze, ribs down, chin tucked, no hyperextension at the top. If your upper back rests against the bench pad in a way that presses on the sore spot, add a towel or shift the pad down. No machine here? Smith at 65-70 per side.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.note: You did 70 x 12 then 75 x 10 with two in reserve on Sunday, so 75 for three sets of 12 is the honest next step. Controlled both directions, no slamming the stack, brief squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Scapular Rehab Block - PAIN-FREE ONLY
exercises.detail: 2 rounds: Band Pull-Apart x 20 (light), Prone Y-Raise bodyweight x 12, Wall Slide x 10
exercises.note: This is treatment for the strained area, not training. Day 4 on a muscle strain is when gentle blood flow starts helping rather than hurting. LIGHT band, no load on the Y-raise, full range, slow. The rule is absolute: pain-free or you stop. A dull working sensation is fine, anything sharp means skip it and tell me. These target lower trap and the scapular stabilizers, which is the tissue that has now failed twice.

exercises.name: Core Circuit
exercises.detail: 2 rounds: Dead Bugs x 12/side, Bird Dog x 10/side, Supported Knee Raise x 15
exercises.note: No side planks today - propping on your elbow loads the shoulder girdle on the side that hurts. Everything here is anti-extension and back-safe with no scapular demand. Lower back flat on the dead bugs, reach long not high on the bird dogs, pause a second at full extension. Use the back-supported knee raise station, not the hanging bar - hanging puts traction straight through the strained area.
